title: Clocking in as president of the Jeff Kready Fan Club  #MasqueradeNYC ...
transcript: Can we just talk about the range required to go from playing The Phantom of the opera to Hester in Operation Midspeed? Because if you didn't see, Jeff Crady, who just got done a run playing The Phantom of the opera in masquerade, was just announced to be the next Hester on Broadway. This is the role originated by Jack Balone. Jack won the Tony for it. But I truly cannot think of two more different roles in musical theatre canon than the Phantom and Hester. The Phantom is brooding and dramatic, whereas Hester is sweet and poised. Like, I guess they both like writing Love Letters, but that's really where the similarities stop. And I do think this kind of range is necessary when doing a show like Operation Mincemeat. All five actors in the show play multiple characters. So, like, this track is not just Hester, but you're also playing Spilsbury and Willy Watkins. And Jeff absolutely has that range. Like, he played Jean Valjean on Broadway at age, like, 24. He covered Santino and Tootsie. He covered Jeremy Jordan and Gatsby. He, of course, most recently played Phantom of the opera. Like, he can do it all. So, yeah, I think he is a perfect fit for the show and this role, and I cannot wait to see what he does with it.
classificationReason: Casting news and reaction to Jeff Kready being announced as the next Hester in Operation Mincemeat on Broadway. Discusses his range and fit for the role but contains no first-hand attendance or opinion about the production itself.
